Aswan

Upper/Middle Nile Valley · Almost entirely irrigated from the Nile system; conjunctive groundwater use in some areas. Irrigation efficiency and drainage are major constraints.

Regional soil: Nile alluvial and desert-fringe sandy soils; very hot, hyper-arid climate.

Rotation context: Winter cereals and berseem clover commonly alternate with summer maize, sorghum, cotton or vegetables. Sugarcane is important in the southern governorates.

explanation.text:
Factor explanations, method and sources
Water balance — 100/100 (user inputs + reference traits)
Mean water-demand level 1.00 on a 1–4 scale (Barley=1, Sorghum=1, Chickpea=1, Sesame=1).

Rule: Mean crop water-demand level (1 very low … 4 very high) is inverted to 0–100. Rainfed systems lose 20 points if any crop needs medium or more water; drip/sprinkler systems receive a 5-point efficiency credit, capped at 100.

Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 crop characteristics; user irrigation inputs.

Sensitivity: ±8 points at this factor level; weight 47.619%.

Salinity fit — 42/100 (user EC + reference thresholds)
Field EC 10 dS/m compared with each crop's approximate ECe threshold.
Below threshold: Barley (8.0 dS/m), Sorghum (6.8 dS/m), Chickpea (1.0 dS/m), Sesame (1.0 dS/m).

Rule: Each crop's approximate ECe tolerance threshold is compared with the user-supplied EC: score = clamp(tolerance / EC, 0, 1) × 100, averaged across crops. Without an EC value the factor uses mean tolerance alone, is marked lower-confidence, and does not pretend to know the field's salinity.

Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 salinity thresholds; user soil test.

Sensitivity: ±8 points at this factor level; weight 0%.

Climate resilience — 80/100 (NASA POWER + reference traits)
Heat pressure 1.00 from 52 day(s) ≥35 °C; rain-scarcity pressure 1.00 (0.0 mm rain over 90 days).
Crop heat tolerance 3.5/5 → component 70.0; drought tolerance 4.5/5 → component 90.0.

Rule: NASA POWER daily maximum temperature and precipitation are reduced to heat-day and rain-scarcity pressures (0–1). For each pressure, the tolerance shortfall from 5/5 is scaled by that pressure and averaged across heat and drought. Without climate data the raw trait score is retained at reduced confidence with no claim of local calibration.

Source: NASA POWER daily AG/LST point data; FAO EcoCrop-derived crop traits.

Sensitivity: ±8 points at this factor level; weight 19.0476%.

Soil protection — 31/100 (reference traits + user organic matter)
Mean cover/residue level 1.50 on a 1–3 scale (cover 1, 2, 1, 1; residue 2, 3, 1, 1).
Organic matter 0.3% (<1%): up to +10 points for residue cover on a depleted soil (qualitative rule).

Rule: Crop soil-cover and residue levels (low/medium/high) are averaged and scaled to 0–100. When user organic matter is below 1%, high-residue crops receive a transparency-flagged bonus because cover is more valuable on depleted soils. This is a qualitative rule, not a soil-carbon model.

Source: Crop trait reference set; user organic-matter input.

Sensitivity: ±10 points at this factor level; weight 14.2857%.

Rotation diversity & continuity — 75.5/100 (reference traits)
1/4 crops fix nitrogen (share 25%; ideal 20–50%).
3/4 distinct crop families.
1 adjacent same-family pair(s): −12 each.
Winter/summer seasons alternate.

Rule: Scores legume presence, distinct crop families, adjacent same-family penalties and winter/summer alternation. It is an agronomic heuristic, not a pest-risk model.

Source: FAO crop rotation principles; crop family and cycle traits.

Sensitivity: ±5 points at this factor level; weight 19.0476%.

Why this sequence: Prioritises low water demand, drought and heat tolerance, and a winter legume. It trades some soil cover and market diversity for lower irrigation exposure.

Caution: Lower water demand does not guarantee savings without matched irrigation scheduling.

methods.text:
Independent prototype — NASA does not endorse this application.

Field Shift is an Egypt-focused decision-support prototype built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It separates measured data, satellite/model estimates, user inputs and calculated indicators.

DATA PROVENANCE

NASA sources and what each one contributes
Official product links
SOURCE	ROLE HERE	RESOLUTION	COVERAGE	ACCESS	OFFICIAL LINKS
NASA POWER — Daily Point API	Temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, humidity, wind and model root-zone wetness for the selected coordinate.	0.5° × 0.5° grid cell (daily point API)	1981-01-01 to near real time; several days latency	Public, no login	Product
Documentation
NASA SMAP — SPL3SMP_E V006	Satellite soil-moisture context. This MVP displays public GIBS imagery and CMR granule metadata; it does not claim a numeric SMAP point value.	9 km enhanced L3 product	Global daily product; imagery dates depend on GIBS processing	Imagery/metadata public; quantitative granules require Earthdata Login	Product
Documentation
NASA GPM IMERG Late Run — GPM_3IMERGDL V07	Precipitation context. Public GIBS imagery and CMR granule metadata; quantitative access is not enabled.	0.1° × 0.1°	Global, 2000-present (Late Run); latest granule verified during development	Imagery/metadata public; quantitative granules require Earthdata Login	Product
Documentation
NASA MODIS — MOD13Q1 V061	Vegetation-index context. Public GIBS NDVI imagery and CMR granule metadata; quantitative access is not enabled.	250 m, 16-day composite	Global, 2000-present	Imagery/metadata public; quantitative granules require Earthdata Login	Product
Documentation

Retrieval timestamps, observation dates and unit metadata are stored with every NASA POWER response and shown in the Climate tab and local SQLite database. NASA GIBS/CMR checks are timestamped in the Satellite tab.

EVIDENCE TYPES

What is measured, modelled, entered or calculated
NASA observation / model estimate
Grid-cell climate and imagery

POWER variables are assimilated/model-derived estimates for a grid cell, not an on-farm sensor reading. SMAP, GPM and MODIS cards show rendered NASA GIBS imagery and verify that CMR granules exist; they do not display a numeric satellite value.

User input
Soil and farm context

Texture, pH, organic matter, EC, drainage, irrigation and water source are entered by the user and stored locally in SQLite. Blank fields remain blank; they are not filled with regional averages.

Reference dataset
Egyptian governorate and crop traits

Governorate summaries and crop characteristics are curated reference ranges from FAO sources. They are not a farm soil test, variety trial or official governorate statistic. The application labels them as reference data wherever they appear.

Calculated indicator
Risk screens, rotation scores and soil classes

Climate-risk signals, factor scores, weighted totals, sensitivity bands and rotation briefs are deterministic rules applied to the inputs above. They are exploratory indicators, not forecasts, official warnings, yield, profit, water-use or food-security predictions.

CLIMATE-RISK SCREENING

Five fixed rules, every threshold visible
Signals and thresholds
Heat stress — days with T2M_MAX ≥35 °C; high at ≥30% of valid days or ≥3 days ≥40 °C.
Dry spell — days with PRECTOTCORR <1 mm; high at ≥90% of days or a run ≥30 days.
Heavy rain — days ≥10 mm; high at ≥3 such days.
Strong wind — days with WS2M ≥6 m/s; high at ≥20% of valid days.
Low humidity — days with mean RH2M <20%; high at ≥30% of valid days.
What the screen does and does not mean

Each card reports the observed count, the longest run where relevant, the source variable and a caveat. Coverage below 80% is stated and lowers confidence. Missing days are excluded, never replaced with zero or a regional average.

The screen describes the selected historical period. It is not a forecast, an official meteorological warning or a crop-loss model. Rain is not irrigation, and air temperature alone does not measure crop heat stress; growth stage, humidity, wind, soil water and management also matter.

The heat and dry-spell pressures use the same POWER inputs as the rotation climate-resilience factor, but the screen does not change the user's weights automatically.

ROTATION METHOD

Five factors, configurable weights, explicit uncertainty
Factors
Water balance — crop water-demand levels against the stated irrigation system.
Salinity fit — crop ECe thresholds against user EC, or a lower-confidence tolerance-only score.
Climate resilience — crop heat/drought traits against NASA POWER heat-day and rain-scarcity pressures.
Soil protection — cover/residue traits with an organic-matter caveat.
Diversity & continuity — legume share, family diversity and season alternation.
Uncertainty and limitations

The displayed range propagates independent factor uncertainty: σ = √Σ(weight × uncertainty)², shown as an 80% sensitivity band. It is not a calibrated confidence interval.

The ranking can change when weights change; a small score gap is not a decisive recommendation. Crop traits vary by variety, soil and management. Local trials and extension advice take precedence.

score = Σ(normalised weight × factor score) / Σ weights of available factors

Crop and salinity references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Papers 56 and 29, FAO EcoCrop and FAO Crop Calendar. Governorate context is a regional synthesis with source links in the Farm tab.

The decision brief reports the leader-to-runner gap, band separation, the strongest and weakest contributing factors, per-scenario risk flags below 50/100, and missing-input checks. Band overlap is a sensitivity check, not a statistical confidence interval or a probability of better performance.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS

What this MVP does not do
Data and access
No quantitative SMAP, GPM or MODIS point extraction: NASA Earthdata Login is required and no credentials are requested or stored.
No farm sensors, field boundaries, yield records or economic data.
POWER is a grid-cell product with several days of latency; it is not local weather-station data.
Climate-risk thresholds are fixed screening rules, not locally calibrated forecasts or official warnings.
Governorate reference data are regional syntheses, not farm measurements.
Scientific scope
No yield, profit, water-saving or soil-carbon prediction is made.
No pesticide, fertilizer or irrigation schedule is prescribed.
Egyptian crop rules are deliberately not transferred outside Egypt.
Rotation scenarios are editable examples, not recommendations.

TRANSPARENCY

AI usage and challenge alignment
Official challenge ↗
AI usage disclosure

AI assistance (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free via the OpenCode coding agent) was used to help write application code, tests, interface text and documentation. AI output was checked against the cited NASA, FAO and geospatial sources and against live API responses.

AI-generated text is not presented as a verified scientific finding. Agricultural assumptions remain simplified reference rules and require specialist review before real-world use. NASA branding is not used to imply endorsement.

Challenge mapping

NASA Earth observations → POWER climate, GIBS/CMR satellite context. Local soil information → user soil profile and governorate reference context. Crop characteristics → 22-crop reference trait set. Farmer priorities → configurable factor weights. Rotation exploration → four transparent scenarios.

See the project README for the full requirement-to-feature audit and test commands.
